name: Biometric verification based on oral cavity
shortDescription: Biometric verification technology that is based on actively mapping the oral cavity by transmitting an audio signal and recording its reflections. It can be integrated into existing products like electronic cigarettes, breath inhalers etc.  Or used a stand alone. Its proven accuracy in a controlled test over more than a 100 subjects was 90% increasing to 95 if using 5 consecutive inhales.
implementationMethodology: Implementation begins by integrating and calibrating a miniaturized acoustic emitter and microphone within the target device or standalone unit to ensure reliable signal capture. During enrollment, users complete a guided inhale sequence while the system emits audio signals, records oral cavity reflections, and converts the normalized acoustic patterns into secure biometric templates. For verification, new inhale samples are assessed through signal quality and noise-handling checks, then matched against the stored template using pattern-recognition algorithms, with optional multi-inhale validation to raise confidence and accuracy. The rollout is supported by controlled testing, firmware and software tuning, and compliance measures suited to medical and consumer deployment within a 3 to 6 month implementation window.
requiredResources: Miniaturized acoustic emitter and microphone hardware, device integration engineering for inhalers e-cigarettes or standalone units, embedded firmware and signal processing software, biometric matching algorithms and secure template storage, calibration tools and validation test fixtures, controlled user trial and performance testing access, cross-functional hardware software QA and compliance team, regulatory and data privacy support
previousImplementations: Previously implemented in controlled validation trials with more than 100 subjects, where the oral-cavity acoustic biometric achieved 90% verification accuracy, increasing to 95% when five consecutive inhales were used. The solution has also been developed for integration into inhale-based devices such as breath inhalers and electronic cigarettes, as well as in standalone prototype configurations for biometric enrollment and verification testing.

name: AssessAI for Education
shortDescription: An institutional AI-powered platform for reviewing, grading, and evaluating student assignments, exams, and written submissions at scale. The solution is designed for universities, colleges, schools, and professional training organizations seeking to reduce the growing administrative burden on lecturers, examiners, and academic staff while improving consistency, speed, and transparency in assessment processes. By automating repetitive evaluation tasks and supporting rubric-based marking, feedback generation, plagiarism indicators, and quality assurance workflows, the platform helps educators focus more on teaching, mentoring, and academic judgment rather than manual checking. It is particularly valuable in environments with large cohorts, limited faculty capacity, and increasing expectations for timely, fair, and data-informed assessment. The importance of this challenge lies in balancing operational efficiency with academic integrity, pedagogical quality, and institutional trust, making AI-enabled assessment a critical capability for the future of education.
implementationMethodology: Implementation follows a phased institutional rollout over 6 to 12 months, starting with assessment policy review, rubric standardization, and integration planning across LMS, SIS, and examination workflows. Historical anonymized submissions and marking data are used to calibrate models, align grading with faculty expectations, and validate fairness, consistency, and academic integrity controls. A pilot is then launched in selected courses with human-in-the-loop review, plagiarism checks, and QA checkpoints before scaling to broader deployment with staff training, governance, audit trails, and continuous performance monitoring.
requiredResources: Executive sponsor, academic assessment leads and faculty subject matter experts, IT team with LMS/SIS integration support, historical anonymized marking data and sample submissions, data governance/compliance and academic integrity oversight, pilot group of lecturers/examiners/administrators for validation, secure cloud or on-premise infrastructure with identity management, training and change management capacity
previousImplementations: Previous implementations have included pilot and phased rollouts across higher education and professional training environments, particularly in institutions managing large student cohorts and high assessment volumes. Typical deployments have focused on rubric-based marking, AI-assisted feedback generation, plagiarism flagging, and moderation support within existing LMS and examination workflows. Early implementations have demonstrated value in reducing marking turnaround times, improving consistency across assessors, and strengthening auditability through human-in-the-loop review and governance controls. These implementations have generally progressed from selected course pilots to broader institutional adoption following calibration, faculty validation, and fairness monitoring.

name: iOS Accessibility Development SDK
shortDescription:
An iOS Accessibility Development SDK for native Swift applications, designed to help teams build truly inclusive mobile experiences from the start rather than treating accessibility as a late-stage compliance task. Many iOS products still present barriers for users who rely on VoiceOver, Dynamic Type, Switch Control, captions, reduced motion, high contrast, and other assistive technologies. This solution addresses that gap by providing developers with reusable components, implementation patterns, testing support, and best-practice guidance tailored for modern Swift-based app development.

The target audience includes iOS engineers, product teams, accessibility specialists, QA teams, and organizations that want to improve usability for people with visual, auditory, motor, or cognitive disabilities while also strengthening overall product quality. The SDK is intended for teams building consumer, enterprise, healthcare, education, finance, and public-sector applications where accessibility is both a user need and a business priority. By making accessible development faster, more consistent, and easier to adopt at scale, this solution helps organizations reduce risk, expand reach, and create better digital experiences for everyone.
requiredResources: plug & play by an iOS junior dev
previousImplementations: Previous implementations have included pilot and production use in native Swift applications where teams needed to improve VoiceOver navigation, Dynamic Type support, semantic labeling, color contrast handling, reduced motion behavior, and assistive technology compatibility across core user journeys. The approach has been applied to reusable component libraries, accessibility remediation programs, and CI-supported testing workflows for iPhone and iPad experiences, helping engineering and QA teams standardize accessible patterns and scale adoption across ongoing releases.

name: CBM - Complete Blood Morphology
shortDescription:
CBM - Complete Blood Morphology is  advanced automation solution designed for hematology laboratories to fully digitize and autonomously perform the peripheral blood smear review process. Today, smear review remains a labor-intensive, manual, and highly specialized workflow that depends on trained professionals to examine blood cell morphology, identify abnormalities, and support clinical decision-making. This creates challenges related to staffing shortages, variability between reviewers, turnaround times, and scalability in high-volume lab environments.

Our solution addresses this critical bottleneck by enabling a fully autonomous review process with no human intervention required in routine analysis. CBM is built for clinical laboratories, hospital hematology departments, and diagnostic centers seeking to improve efficiency, standardization, and operational capacity while maintaining high-quality diagnostic performance. By automating this essential step, the platform has the potential to reduce workload, minimize subjectivity, accelerate reporting, and support more consistent patient care. This is especially important as laboratories face rising demand, increasing complexity, and ongoing pressure to do more with fewer skilled resources.
implementationMethodology: CBM is implemented as a fully digital morphology workflow that scans peripheral blood smears at 100x magnification and analyzes thousands of white blood cells, red blood cells, and platelets per sample. Using advanced AI models, the platform classifies more than 20 WBC categories and delivers significantly expanded RBC and platelet morphology characterization compared with conventional manual review. The system automatically generates a standardized, clinically actionable report, enabling autonomous routine smear assessment with high consistency and speed. This methodology modernizes morphology review in the same way CBC analyzers transformed hematology in the 1970s, bringing scalable automation, reproducibility, and improved laboratory efficiency.
previousImplementations: CBM is currently being evaluated in clinical trials across multiple sites worldwide, with additional evaluation agreements in place with leading reference laboratories in the United States and Europe.

shortDescription: Permitting Issuing For Construction addresses one of the most persistent bottlenecks in construction delivery: the slow, fragmented, and error-prone process of preparing, reviewing, approving, and issuing permit packages for construction. Project teams often manage drawings, revisions, compliance requirements, agency comments, and internal approvals across disconnected tools, creating delays, rework, missed deadlines, and increased project risk. This solution is intended for developers, architects, engineers, general contractors, permit coordinators, and municipal or regulatory stakeholders who need a more reliable and transparent path from design completion to construction authorization. The challenge is especially important in complex projects where multiple disciplines, jurisdictions, and approval gates must be aligned before work can begin. A strong solution should improve document control, workflow visibility, accountability, and turnaround time while reducing administrative burden and compliance gaps. By streamlining permitting and IFC issuance, organizations can accelerate project starts, improve collaboration, and lower the operational and financial impact of approval delays.
requiredResources: Required resources include a cross-functional team of BIM modelers, architects, engineers, permit coordinators, document controllers, and project managers, supported by municipal and regulatory contacts. Core technology should include a 3D BIM environment, common data environment, drawing and revision control system, workflow automation, approval tracking, and reporting dashboards. Access to current codes, jurisdictional submission standards, template permit packages, and IFC checklists is essential. Implementation also requires data migration from legacy files, integration with design and project management tools, user training, governance rules, and executive sponsorship to drive adoption, accountability, and turnaround time improvements.

name: Next-Generation Natural Killer Cell Immunotherapy: Modulation of Intracellular Inhibitory Checkpoints
shortDescription:
We have developed a next-generation immunotherapeutic platform designed to enhance the natural cytotoxic activity of Natural Killer (NK) cells against cancer and virally infected cells by suppressing key intracellular inhibitory checkpoints. Despite the strong promise of NK cell-based therapies, many current approaches are limited by complex cell isolation and expansion procedures, variable potency, and reduced functional persistence. Our strategy directly modulates the internal regulatory mechanisms that restrain NK cell killing, enabling stronger anti-tumor and antiviral responses both ex vivo and in vivo while addressing several practical and biological limitations of existing NK cell immunotherapies.

This solution is highly relevant to biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies, immuno-oncology developers, cell therapy groups, and partners seeking broadly applicable immune-based platforms. Because NK cells play a central role in surveillance against malignant and infected cells, this technology has potential utility across a wide range of solid tumors, hematological cancers, and viral infections. By improving NK cell efficacy through a targeted intracellular mechanism, our approach offers a promising path toward more potent, scalable, and clinically meaningful immunotherapies.
implementationMethodology: The solution will be advanced through completion of late preclinical validation using established in vitro, cell culture, and animal model systems to confirm enhanced NK cell cytotoxicity, persistence, and safety after modulation of intracellular inhibitory checkpoints. Based on the target indication and partner strategy, the platform can be developed as either an off-the-shelf or personalized NK cell therapy, followed by process optimization, cGMP manufacturing setup, and IND-enabling studies. BIRAD Research and Development Company will support intellectual property protection, partner engagement, and commercialization planning as the program progresses toward clinical trial entry.
requiredResources: Preclinical funding of approximately 1.75 million USD, followed by additional funding for IND-enabling clinical, cGMP manufacturing infrastructure partner, clinical development partner for first-in-human trial preparation and / or Phase I/IIa.
previousImplementations: In-vitro, cell culture, animal models are all well established
